children: subsidiary African Metals has received approval from Botswana’s Department of Mines to excavate shallow exploration pits at the Airstrip and Dibete copper-silver prospects in the nation’s east.
The 10-metre deep pits are designed to expose near-surface oxide and supergene copper-silver mineralisation outlined by previous drilling, trenching, and historical workings.

The excavation of two initial pits will allow detailed mapping and sampling of the structures that control localised high-grade shoots and will provide up to 100 tonnes of oxidised material for metallurgical test work.

The pits form part of an exploration pitting and bulk sampling program across Verity’s wholly owned 2,868-square-kilometre Botswana portfolio, following the acquisition of BCL Investments’ joint venture interest in December.

Airstrip C6 will sit directly above previous drilling on the C6 shoot, which returned intercepts of 11 metres at 7.63% copper and 462g/t silver from 52m including 3m at 22.74% copper and 1,379g/t silver.

The Dibete pit will cover historical copper workings and previous drilling collared within the pit footprint with best assays of 10m at 2.04% copper and 15.6g/t silver from 7m and 25m at 2.17% copper and 77g/t silver from 27m.
Director Patrick Volpe said approval to open the first exploration pits at Airstrip and Dibete was an important practical step for the Botswana copper-silver portfolio.

“For the first time we will expect to see the near-surface mineralisation exposed in the walls and floor of a pit, rather than inferred from drill holes, and we will map the structures that control the high-grade shoots,” he said.

“The pits will give us enough material to run proper metallurgical test work on the oxide and supergene copper at both prospects—understanding how that material responds to processing will be a key input to deciding the next phase of work."
The Airstrip and Dibete prospects lie approximately 6.5 kilometres apart along the Magogophate Shear Zone in the high-grade Limpopo Mobile Belt.

The new pits will be used for exploration only, with the goal of exposing near-surface mineralisation and its contacts with host and country rocks for detailed geological mapping and structural interpretation.
They will also allow for systematic channel and bench sampling to compare with nearby drill results; and provide bulk samples of oxidised material for metallurgical and mineralogical testwork.

Each pit will be excavated from the top down in two 5m benches by a local earthmoving contractor using an excavator and articulated dump truck, with material to be stockpiled at least 5m from the pit edge.

Mineralised material from each bench will be kept separate and waste stockpiled for later rehabilitation, while the pit walls and floor will be geologically logged and sampled for analysis at accredited laboratory SGS South Africa.

title: Verity Resources Gains Approval for Exploration Pits at Airstrip and Dibete Copper-Silver Prospects in Botswana
